title: Isolation of mouse senescence-associated CD4+ T cells using flow cytometry
author: Fukushima, Minato, et al.

steps.title: Coat 96-well plate with antibodies
steps.instruction: Dilute anti‑CD3ε to 10 µg/mL in PBS for condition A; for condition B dilute anti‑CD3ε to 10 µg/mL and anti‑CD153 to 25 µg/mL (or anti‑CD3ε + rat IgG 25 µg/mL for negative control). Add 100 µL of each diluted antibody solution to the appropriate wells of a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate; add 200 µL PBS to the outer wells to prevent evaporation. Wrap the plate with plastic wrap and incubate at 4 °C for 16–20 h.

substeps.instruction: Prepare antibody dilutions in PBS as described.
Dispense 100 µL of each dilution into designated wells.
Add 200 µL PBS to outer wells.
Wrap plate and incubate 4 °C 16–20 h.

steps.title: Purify CD4+ T cells from spleen
steps.instruction: Sacrifice two mice per pooled sample by CO₂ asphyxiation, spray with alcohol, and collect spleens into a 70 µm cell strainer on a 6 cm petri dish containing 5 mL FACS buffer. Mash spleens with a sterile 1 mL syringe plunger, wash with an additional 5 mL FACS buffer, and transfer the 10 mL suspension to a 15 mL conical tube. Centrifuge 350 × g 5 min at 4 °C and aspirate supernatant. Lyse red blood cells by resuspending the pellet in 2 mL ACK lysis buffer, incubating 2 min at 20–25 °C, then adding 10 mL FACS buffer, mixing, and centrifuging 350 × g 5 min at 4 °C; aspirate supernatant. Block Fc receptors by resuspending cells in 5 mL anti‑CD16/32 (2.4G2) supernatant, incubating 15 min at 4 °C, centrifuging 350 × g 5 min at 4 °C, and aspirating. (Optional count). Label CD4⁺ cells with CD4 MicroBeads: dilute 200 µL beads to 2 mL MACS buffer, add to cells, incubate 30 min at 4 °C, add 10 mL MACS buffer, invert, centrifuge 350 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate, and resuspend in 1 mL MACS buffer. Perform magnetic separation using an LS column rinsed with 3 mL MACS buffer, load the cell suspension, wash column twice with 3 mL MACS buffer, remove column from magnet, flush labeled CD4⁺ cells with 5 mL MACS buffer into a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 350 × g 5 min at 4 °C, and aspirate supernatant. (Optional count).

substeps.instruction: Sacrifice mice, disinfect, and collect spleens into FACS buffer.
Mash spleens, wash, and centrifuge.
Lyse red blood cells with ACK buffer.
Block Fc receptors with anti‑CD16/32.
Label cells with CD4 MicroBeads.
Magnetically separate CD4⁺ cells using LS column.

steps.title: Stain cells for flow sorting
steps.instruction: Resuspend the purified cells in 300 µL of staining panel A or B (each antibody at 1:200 dilution in FACS buffer), incubate 20 min in the dark at 4 °C, add 10 mL FACS buffer, invert to mix, centrifuge 350 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, resuspend in 1–2 mL FACS buffer, and filter the suspension through a 35 µm strainer cap into a 5 mL polystyrene tube kept on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL staining panel to cells.
Incubate 20 min, dark, 4 °C.
Wash with 10 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge.
Resuspend in 1–2 mL FACS buffer.
Filter through 35 µm cap.

steps.title: Prepare cytometer and collection tubes
steps.instruction: Power on the flow cytometer, run CS&T beads to check performance, determine drop delay with Accudrop beads, and install a 70 µm or 85 µm nozzle. Prepare 10 mL culture medium in 15 mL conical tubes, coat the interior surface of each tube with the medium, and place the tubes on a two‑way 15 mL collection device. Immediately before loading the sample, add 1/200 volume of 100 µg/mL propidium iodide to the sample tube and vortex to stain dead cells.

substeps.instruction: Set up cytometer (CS&T beads, drop delay, nozzle).
Prepare 10 mL culture medium in 15 mL tubes and coat interior.
Place tubes on collection device.
Add PI (1/200 of 100 µg/mL) to sample tube and vortex.

steps.title: Sort CD153+ SA-T cells
steps.instruction: Set the sample temperature control to 4 °C. Choose gating strategy A (straight) or B (enrichment). Load the appropriate stained sample (panel A for A, panel B for B) onto the cytometer. For strategy A, sort CD153⁺ SA‑T cells (CD153⁺ PD‑1⁺ CD44hi CD4⁺ B220⁻ CD11b⁻) into one collection tube and PD‑1⁻ CD44hi CD4⁺ cells (CD153⁻ PD‑1⁻ CD44hi) into a second tube. For strategy B, sort enriched CD153⁺ SA‑T cells (Lag3⁺ CD121b⁻ CD25⁻ PD‑1⁺ CD44hi CD4⁺ B220⁻ CD11b⁻) and the corresponding PD‑1⁻ CD44hi (Lag3⁻ CD121b⁻ CD25⁻) population. Collect at least 1.5 × the desired number of cells. After sorting, unload the sample tube, mix the collection medium with a sterile 1000 µL tip, take ~200 µL aliquot, reload it onto the cytometer, and re‑analyze to confirm >90 % of events fall within the target gate. Record the total sort count displayed on the Sort Layout Window.

substeps.instruction: Set sample temperature to 4 °C.
Select gating strategy and load appropriate stained sample.
Sort target populations into separate collection tubes.
Collect ≥1.5 × desired cell number.
Verify purity by re‑analysis of an aliquot.
Record total sort count.

steps.title: Centrifuge and adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sorted cells at 350 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, then repeat centrifugation for 5 min at 4 °C and aspirate again to remove residual liquid. Resuspend the pellet in culture medium to an estimated concentration of 2 × 10⁶ cells/mL based on the total sort count (e.g., 300 µL medium for 6 × 10⁵ cells). Count the cells by mixing 10 µL of suspension with 10 µL 0.4 % Trypan Blue, loading 10 µL into a hemocytometer, counting live (unstained) cells, and calculating the actual concentration. Adjust the suspension to 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL by adding culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 15 min, aspirate, repeat 5 min, aspirate.
Resuspend to ~2 × 10⁶ cells/mL based on sort count.
Perform Trypan Blue count and calculate actual concentration.
Dilute to 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL with medium.

steps.title: Stimulate cells on coated plate
steps.instruction: Dilute anti‑CD28 antibody 1:250 in culture medium to obtain a 2× solution containing 4 µg/mL anti‑CD28. Remove the coating solution and PBS from each well of the pre‑coated 96‑well plate. Add 50 µL of the 2× anti‑CD28 solution to wells designated for CD3ε/CD28 stimulation (blue and magenta wells) and add 50 µL of plain culture medium to wells designated for CD3ε/CD28/CD153 stimulation (yellow wells). Add 50 µL of the cell suspension (1 × 10⁶ cells/mL) to each well, giving a final volume of 100 µL per well. Incubate the plate at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator. Use any remaining cells for additional assays such as cytokine FACS, survival assays, or RNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 2× anti‑CD28 solution (4 µg/mL).
Aspirate coating solution and PBS from wells.
Add 50 µL anti‑CD28 solution to CD3ε/CD28 wells; add 50 µL medium to CD3ε/CD28/CD153 wells.
Add 50 µL cell suspension to each well (final 100 µL).
Incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

description: Senescence-associated (SA) T cells were initially identified as programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1+) CD44hi CD4+ T cells.2 Recently, however, SA-T cells expressing CD153 (CD153+ SA-T cells) have garnered increasing attention because of their potential relationship to the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease.1,3,4,5,6,7 In response to T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation, CD153+ SA-T cells have diminished proliferation capacity and produce large amounts of a proinflammatory cytokine osteopontin (OPN), at the cost of typical T cell cytokines such as interleukin 2 (IL-2). Interestingly, concomitant engagement of CD153 enhances TCR signaling and upregulates the proliferation capacity and cytokine production of CD153+ SA-T cells. This protocol describes the isolation and subsequent evaluation of CD153+ SA-T cells. Specifically, CD153+ SA-T cells were isolated from spleens using a flow cytometry-based method, and the TCR-mediated response was assessed in vitro using plate-bound anti-CD3ε (a component of the TCR) and soluble anti-CD28 antibodies (Abs) (Figures 1A and 1B). The additional presence of plate-bound anti-CD153 Ab (clone RM153) served to recapitulate the enhancement of TCR signaling (Figure 1B).Figure 1Plate layout for in vitro stimulation(A) Example of a 96-well plate layout for stimulation via CD3ε/CD28 (n = 3). S1 and C1 indicate wells for CD153+ SA-T cells and PD-1– CD44hi cells, respectively. S2/3 and C2/3 indicate wells for biological replicates of S1 and C1, respectively.(B) Example of a 96-well plate layout for stimulation via CD3ε/CD28/CD153 (n = 3). S1 and C1 indicate wells for enriched CD153+ SA-T cells and PD-1– CD44hi (Lag3– CD121b– CD25–) cells, respectively. S2/3 and C2/3 indicate wells for biological replicates of S1 and C1, respectively.(A and B) The diluted Abs or buffers and corresponding well positions are shown in the same color.
